newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coplex, Dolphin in MidEast oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Coplex, Dolphin in MidEast oil deal.

text.p: Coplex Resources NL said on Monday it had reached agreement with Canadian-based Dolphin Quest Ltd amalgamate with Naftex Energy Ltd, its wholly-owned Canadian subsidiary which owns two of Coplex's subsidiaries.

The subsidiaries, Coplex (East Shabwa) Ltd and Coplex (Egypt) Ltd, hold a five percent interest in the East Shabwa Contract Area in Yemen and a 50 percent interest in the West Esh El Mallaha Concession in Egypt respectively.

Coplex said that as part of the deal Dolphin Quest, which is quoted on the electronic Canadian Dealing Network, engaged Canaccord Capital Corp to arrange a financing to initially raise sufficient funds to complete the East Shabwa Development Programme in Yemen and to proceed with the drilling of up to two wells in the West Esh El Mallaha Concession in Egypt.
"Canaccord has advised Coplex management that the financing, structured as a special warrants issue, is substantially over-subscribed," Coplex said.

The structure of the special warrant financing arranged by Canaccord is for each special warrant to be converted into one share at a price of C$0.45 cents with an attaching one-half share purchase warrant.
Each whole warrant entitles the holder to acquire one fully paid share at a price of C$0.55 cents per share, exercisable within a 15-month period.
Conversion of the special warrants will be automatic immediately prior to completion of the amalgamation.
"As a result of this financing, Dolphin Quest (which is to be renamed Naftex Energy Corp - will have approximately C$7.2 million (A$6.9 million) in cash and no debt," Coplex said.
"A further C$10.7 million (A$ 10.0 million) will be injected into Naftex if the share purchase warrants are fully exercised," the company said.

Coplex said the initial tranche of funds adequately covered the costs of Naftex's five percent share of the East Shabwa Development Programme and provides funding for Naftex's 50 percent share of up to two wells to be drilled on the West Esh El Mallaha Concession in Egypt in which Naftex will be operator.
"Other opportunities in the Middle East are under review which could, if required, be funded through the exercise of the SharePurchase Warrants," the company said.

Coplex would receive 30 million Naftex shares together with warrants exercisable into a further 10 million Naftex shares. The exercise price is C$0.55 cents per share for the first 15 months and C$0.65 cents a share for the following nine months.
Based on the issue price of C$0.45 cents per share, this initially values Coplex's shareholding in Naftex at C$13.5 million (A$12.6 million), Coplex said.
Coplex said it would retain a 56 percent stake in Naftex.
Coplex shares were trading at 44.5 cents at midday on Monday, up 1.5 cents from Friday's close.
